dbBackup.question: How does Dockstash back up a Docker database?
dbBackup.answer: Dockstash runs the database’s native dump inside the running container (pg_dumpall, mysqldump --single-transaction, or mongodump --oplog), then stores the dump as an encrypted Restic snapshot. It never copies live database files off disk, because a half-written data file cannot be restored.

storage.question: Where are my backups stored?
storage.answer: On your own storage VPS over SSH, as standard encrypted Restic repositories. Dockstash never holds your data. The Free tier runs entirely self-hosted with no paid provider.

restoreProof.question: How do I know a backup will actually restore?
restoreProof.answer: Dockstash runs automated restore drills: it restores the latest snapshot to a scratch location and diffs it against the source, then surfaces per-project drill status. An untested backup is treated as no backup.

config.question: Do I need to write a backup config?
config.answer: No. Dockstash scans your Docker Compose project, detects databases, volumes, and reverse-proxy config, and proposes a plan you confirm with checkboxes. One click backs everything up.

seo.title: Security — how Dockstash protects your data
seo.description: How Dockstash secures backups: AES-256-GCM secrets at rest, SSH host-key pinning, encrypted Restic repositories, typed-confirm restores, restore-drill verification, and no lock-in.

security.title: Security you can verify
security.answer: Dockstash is built to hold your most sensitive credentials safely. Secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, the SSH backup channel pins the storage host key, and every Restic repository is encrypted with your own key. Destructive restores require a typed confirmation, and restore drills prove your data recovers.

secrets.title: AES-256-GCM secrets at rest
secrets.body: Your Restic password and SSH keys are never stored in plaintext. They are encrypted at rest with an AES-256-GCM master key, with recovery-code escrow for key rotation.

pinning.title: SSH host-key pinning
pinning.body: The backup channel to your storage VPS pins the host key, so a man-in-the-middle cannot silently intercept or redirect your encrypted snapshots.

repos.title: Encrypted Restic repositories
repos.body: Every repository is a standard Restic repo encrypted with your key. Data is encrypted and deduplicated before it ever leaves your production VPS.

typedConfirm.title: Typed-confirm destructive restore
typedConfirm.body: A restore that overwrites live data requires you to type the project name to confirm. The default is restore-to-new-location, with database staging before any overwrite.

drills.title: Restore-drill verification
drills.body: Dockstash restores the latest snapshot to a scratch location and diffs it against the source on a schedule, so you find out a backup is broken before you need it.

lockIn.title: Your storage, no lock-in
lockIn.body: Backups live on your own storage VPS as standard Restic repos. If you ever leave, restore with the restic CLI alone — Dockstash adds no proprietary layer.

secrets.question: Where are my SSH key and Restic password stored?
secrets.answer: Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a master key, never in plaintext. On the self-hosted tier they live on your own server. Recovery-code escrow lets you rotate the master key without losing access.

holdData.question: Does Dockstash ever hold my backup data?
holdData.answer: No. On the Free/self-host tier the entire pipeline runs on your infrastructure and backups land on your storage VPS. Dockstash orchestrates the backup; it never stores your data on our servers.

destructive.question: How does Dockstash prevent an accidental destructive restore?
destructive.answer: Restores default to a new location, databases are staged before any overwrite, and a restore that would overwrite live data requires you to type the project name to confirm. There is no one-click way to clobber production.

disappear.question: What happens to my encrypted backups if Dockstash disappears?
disappear.answer: They stay on your storage VPS as standard, encrypted Restic repositories. Point the restic CLI at the repo with your key and restore with no vendor involved. There is zero lock-in.

seo.title: Dockstash FAQ — Docker backup questions
seo.description: Answers to common questions about Dockstash: how it backs up Docker databases, where backups are stored, security, pricing, restore verification, and avoiding lock-in.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.answer: Dockstash is a self-hostable, Docker-aware backup orchestrator. It auto-detects your Compose stack, dumps each database the correct way from its running container, stores encrypted Restic snapshots on your own storage VPS, and drill-tests the restore. Below are the questions we hear most.

what.question: What does Dockstash actually do?
what.answer: It runs on your production VPS, scans your Docker Compose projects, and detects every backup-able layer — volumes, databases, compose/.env, and reverse-proxy config. It dumps databases consistently from the running container, then stores encrypted Restic snapshots off-site over SSH with automated restore-drill verification.

whyNotBackrest.question: Why not just use Backrest?
whyNotBackrest.answer: Backrest is a solid generic restic UI, but it does not know your database needs a pg_dumpall rather than a file copy, it does not detect your Compose stack, and it will not drill-test restores. Dockstash is Docker-project-aware and verifies recovery.

whyNotDiy.question: Why not write my own restic + cron script?
whyNotDiy.answer: You can — and then maintain it, hope the database dumps stay consistent through version bumps, and notice when cron silently stops. Dockstash is that script, hardened, alerted, verified, and reduced to one click.

safe.question: Is my data safe with Dockstash?
safe.answer: On the Free/self-host tier everything runs on your own servers and backups land on your storage VPS — we never hold your data. Secrets are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and Restic repositories are encrypted with your own key.

shutdown.question: What happens if Dockstash shuts down?
shutdown.answer: Your repositories are standard Restic. Point the restic CLI at your storage VPS and restore without us. Config export/import is included, so there is zero lock-in.

restoreProof.question: How do I know my backups will actually restore?
restoreProof.answer: Dockstash runs automated restore drills: it restores the latest snapshot to a scratch location, diffs it against the source, and surfaces per-project drill status. An untested backup is treated as no backup.

engines.question: Which databases does Dockstash support?
engines.answer: Docker-aware adapters cover PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Valkey, SQLite, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ, MinIO, InfluxDB, and Neo4j — each dumped the correct, consistent way for its engine.

config.question: Do I need to write a backup config file?
config.answer: No. Dockstash scans your Compose project, detects databases, volumes, and reverse-proxy config, and proposes a plan you confirm with checkboxes. One click backs everything up — no YAML to author.

storage.question: Where are my backups stored?
storage.answer: On your own storage VPS over SSH, as standard encrypted Restic repositories. The Free tier runs entirely self-hosted with no paid provider, so nothing transits a third party.

cost.question: How much does Dockstash cost?
cost.answer: The Free tier is {{freePrice}} for one self-hosted project. Pro adds {{proProjects}} projects, hourly backups, and email alerts; Business is unlimited projects with priority support and multi-VPS. Yearly billing gives you two months free.

seo.title: Back up every VPS from one dashboard — Dockstash fleet agents
seo.description: Install a lightweight agent on each server and manage all your Docker backups from one place. Outbound-only, no inbound ports, least-privilege Docker access.

hero.subtitle: Drop a lightweight agent on each VPS. It phones home over HTTPS — no inbound ports, no SSH keys handed out — and runs the same restic-backed backups Dockstash runs on your primary host.

register.title: Register the agent
register.body: Add the server in your fleet and copy the one-time token.

install.title: Run one command
install.body: Paste the docker compose one-liner on the VPS. The agent starts with the token baked in.

assign.title: Assign projects
assign.body: Point any project at the agent. Its backups now run on that host and report back live.

install.heading: One command per server
install.body: The agent ships as a Docker image with a bundled least-privilege socket proxy — the same posture as the main stack. No host tooling, no root, no open ports.

multiVps.question: How do I back up multiple VPS servers with one dashboard?
multiVps.answer: Install the Dockstash agent on each server and assign that server’s projects to its agent. Every backup, snapshot, and alert shows up in one fleet view.

rootPorts.question: Does the agent need root or inbound ports?
rootPorts.answer: No. The agent connects outbound to Dockstash over HTTPS, so no inbound ports are opened. It reaches Docker only through a least-privilege socket proxy limited to container exec.

auth.question: How is the agent authenticated?
auth.answer: Each agent gets a one-time composite token stored server-side only as a keyed HMAC. It authenticates every request with that token, and you can rotate or revoke it instantly.

cta.heading: Run one dashboard for your whole fleet
cta.body: Multi-VPS fleet view is on the Business plan.

volumeCopy.question: Why can’t I just copy the database volume?
volumeCopy.answer: A running database writes to its data directory constantly. Copying it mid-write captures a torn, inconsistent state that usually will not restore. The correct backup is a logical dump (pg_dumpall, mysqldump --single-transaction, mongodump --oplog) taken from the running container.

guideVsUseCase.question: What is the difference between a guide and a use-case page?
guideVsUseCase.answer: A guide covers one database engine (how to back up PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, and so on). A use-case page covers a whole app stack (WordPress, n8n, Supabase) — which databases it runs, which volumes hold files, and the full ordered backup plan.

automation.question: Does Dockstash automate all of this?
automation.answer: Yes. Dockstash scans your Compose project, detects the databases, volumes, and config, runs the correct dump per engine, and stores encrypted Restic snapshots off-site — then drill-tests the restore so you know it works.

seo.title: Continuous Docker backups every five minutes — Dockstash
seo.description: Turn on the continuous preset and Dockstash snapshots your Docker project every five minutes — deduplicated restic storage, tiered retention, and restore to any point in time.

hero.subtitle: The continuous preset backs up your project on a 5-minute cadence. Restic deduplication keeps each snapshot tiny, tiered retention collapses the train into hourly and daily keeps, and restore picks the snapshot nearest any timestamp.

cadence.title: 5-minute cadence
cadence.body: Schedules run down to every five minutes on Pro — near-continuous protection without a streaming agent.

dedup.title: Deduplicated storage
dedup.body: Restic uploads only changed blocks, so a 5-minute cadence costs a fraction of repeated full snapshots.

pitr.title: Point-in-time restore
pitr.body: Pick any timestamp; Dockstash resolves the nearest snapshot at or before it and restores it in one click.

retention.title: Tiered retention
retention.body: Keep-last, hourly, daily, weekly and monthly keeps collapse the snapshot train automatically.

enable.title: Enable the preset
enable.body: One click sets the every-five-minutes cron and a tuned retention policy on your project.

accumulate.title: Snapshots accumulate
accumulate.body: Every five minutes the dump-and-snapshot pipeline runs; any failure alerts you immediately.

restore.title: Restore to a moment
restore.body: Enter a timestamp in the PITR tab, confirm the resolved snapshot, and restore.

rpo.question: What RPO does continuous backup give me?
rpo.answer: With the 5-minute preset the worst-case data-loss window is five minutes plus the dump duration. Business plans can schedule down to one minute.

cost.question: Doesn't a 5-minute cadence explode storage costs?
cost.answer: No. Restic deduplicates at the block level, so unchanged data is never re-uploaded, and tiered retention prunes the snapshot train into hourly and daily keeps.

restore.question: How do I restore to a specific time?
restore.answer: Open the project's PITR tab and pick a timestamp. Dockstash resolves the newest snapshot at or before it and shows the exact gap before you confirm.

cta.heading: Shrink your backup window to minutes
cta.body: Continuous backup is included in Pro. Enable the preset on any project in one click.

seo.title: Backup monitoring and alerts for Docker projects — Dockstash
seo.description: A health dashboard for every backup: healthy/degraded/critical project scoring, an in-app alert center, and email plus webhook alerts the moment a backup, restore or drill fails.

hero.subtitle: Backups fail quietly. Dockstash scores every project from real signals — last run, restore drills, repository checks, schedules and agent liveness — and tells you the moment anything drifts.

dashboard.title: Health dashboard
dashboard.body: Every project is scored healthy, degraded or critical from real signals: last run, drills, repo checks, schedules and agent liveness.

alertCenter.title: Alert center
alertCenter.body: Every failure and silent stall is recorded in-app with read/unread state — no alert disappears into a mailbox.

channels.title: Email + webhooks
channels.body: Failure alerts reach your inbox and any per-project webhook — wire up Slack, Discord or PagerDuty in minutes.

heartbeat.title: Dead-man's switch
heartbeat.body: If a project goes quiet past its heartbeat window, Dockstash alerts you even though nothing explicitly "failed".

states.heading: Three states, zero ambiguity
states.body: The fleet banner always shows the worst project, so a single glance answers the only question that matters.

healthy.title: Healthy
healthy.body: Recent successful backup, drills passing, schedule active.

degraded.title: Degraded
degraded.body: Something needs attention: a failed repo check, a missing schedule, or a project that has never run.

critical.title: Critical
critical.body: A failed backup, drill or restore, a stale project past its heartbeat window, or an offline agent.

signals.question: What signals feed the health score?
signals.answer: Last backup result and age, restore-drill and repository-check outcomes, schedule presence, pause state, and the liveness of any assigned fleet agent.

channels.question: Which alert channels are supported?
channels.answer: In-app alerts on every plan, plus email and per-project webhooks on Pro and Business. Webhooks POST JSON, so Slack, Discord and PagerDuty integrations are one URL away.

silent.question: What about silent failures where nothing runs at all?
silent.answer: A dead-man's-switch sweep alerts you whenever a project has had no successful backup inside its heartbeat window — the failure mode most monitoring misses.

cta.heading: Stop hoping. Start knowing.
cta.body: Health scoring and the alert center are built in; email and webhook alerts are included with Pro.

seo.title: One-way directory mirror through encrypted backups — Dockstash
seo.description: Replicate a directory one-way: the source is snapshotted into your encrypted restic repo and restored onto the target on every scheduled run — versioned, verified and allowlisted.

hero.subtitle: Mirror mode replays your source directory onto a target path through the encrypted repo. Unlike rsync, every cycle is a complete, versioned snapshot — and the backup history rides along for free.

oneWay.title: Strictly one-way
oneWay.body: Source to target through the repo — no conflict resolution to reason about, no accidental reverse sync.

pointInTime.title: Point-in-time copies
pointInTime.body: Each cycle restores a complete snapshot, so the target is a consistent moment — never a half-copied tree.

allowlist.title: Allowlisted paths
allowlist.body: Source and target must live inside your project-root allowlist — enforced when you save and again on every run.

scheduled.title: On your schedule
scheduled.body: Runs as a normal scheduled job with the same retries, live logs and failure alerts as backups.

configure.title: Point at two paths
configure.body: Set a source and a target directory on the project — both validated against the allowlist.

schedule.title: Add a schedule
schedule.body: Mirror is a schedulable job kind: hourly, daily, or any cadence your plan allows.

replicate.title: Dockstash replicates
replicate.body: Each run snapshots the source under a mirror tag and restores the latest onto the target.

twoWay.question: Does Dockstash support two-way sync?
twoWay.answer: No — deliberately. Two-way sync needs conflict resolution and can propagate mistakes in both directions. One-way mirroring with full version history is safer and predictable.

deletes.question: How do deletions propagate?
deletes.answer: Every mirror snapshot is complete, so a file removed at the source is absent from the next snapshot — and still recoverable from earlier ones.

plan.question: Which plan includes mirror mode?
plan.answer: Mirror mode is a Business-plan feature, alongside multi-VPS fleet agents and any-cadence scheduling.

cta.heading: Every version, one direction
cta.body: Mirror mode is included in Business. Configure a source and target and add a schedule.
